source.basis: Operator facility page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
At 36 MW of published IT capacity across 358,000 square feet of technical space, this campus is a substantial facility by any measure. To translate that into AI hardware terms, at 40 kW per rack, a common AI training density, 36 MW would support roughly 900 racks; at 10 kW per rack, a more typical enterprise average, the same power would fill about 3,600 racks. Those are assumptions about rack density, not operator claims. What the operator has published is the 36 MW figure, and that number alone places the campus at the top of what this site has measured in Oregon.

The certification stack qualifies this campus for a broad range of regulated workloads. SOC 1 Type 2 and SOC 2 Type 2 cover financial and operational controls auditing. PCI DSS qualifies it for payment card data. ITAR means the facility meets U.S. export-control requirements for defense-related information. NIST 800-53 and HITRUST together cover federal security frameworks and healthcare data. SSAE 18 is the auditing standard under which the SOC reports are issued. Nothing in the published specifications identifies which tenants or workloads are actually present.

Oregon has 133 facilities mapped in this site's dataset, of which only 6 have published a megawatt figure, totaling 182 MW across those six. This campus accounts for 36 of those 182 MW, or roughly 20 percent of all published capacity in the state, and it ranks first among the six by that measure. The remaining 127 mapped facilities publish no capacity figure, so the true state total is unknown. Oregon's grid context is not published in the operator's specifications and is not addressed here.
